meta.title: The Old Town Walk in Six Photos
meta.textType: a short story in words and pictures

paragraphs: On Saturday, the Explorers walked in the old town with Teacher Kim. Mia took six photos with her camera. Lily wrote a short caption under each photo. The captions tell the story of our walk. Please look at the photos one by one.

Photo one. We met at the east gate of the old town at nine o'clock. The gate is old and made of gray stone. Everyone was on time, and Teacher Kim counted us. Photo two. An old red box stood next to the gate. It is still in use today. May wrote a card for Ms. Ong and her class. She posted it in the red box, and we waved to it.

Photo three. Then it began to rain, and the street was wet. No one had an umbrella, so everyone ran under a small roof. Photo four. Instead of a long walk, we entered a small old house. The street was quiet, and there were no cars. The door was green, and the windows were small. It was a museum of old toys, and every shelf was full.

Photo five. A woman and her husband live in the house. He makes the toys, and she is his wife and his helper. The man showed us a small train that he made. Leo pushed an old toy car across the floor. The woman smiled and said, "That car is very old." Photo six. We said thank you, and the rain stopped. We walked back to the east gate in the sun. Mia took the last photo of the old house with the sun on its roof.
"Remember this day," said Teacher Kim. "A small house can be a great place." Lily put the six photos on Explorers' Blog. Which photo do you like best? What do you remember from your last trip?
